facts.fact: 她大学唯一一年在 SUNY Nowhere：二月，她恨那里——习惯处是人、天黑就进屋不出门；但离开城市让眼睛有机会适应空荡，见到第一次真正的显形。
facts.anchor: It felt wrong not to have people around everywhere, to go inside when it got dark and then stay inside.

facts.fact: 入门技法：放松眼睛、让鬼自己浮现而非去抓；若去找他们他们会躲开，看中间距离他们就会经过。
facts.anchor: I tried relaxing my eyes and letting them appear instead of trying to snatch them up, which was eventually the trick.

facts.fact: Mary Ellen Bishop 是人物写生课总坐她邻座、爱说话的同学；第一次男模特时她脸颊胸口耳朵热红——「我」觉她并非紧张而是自洽，这反而让「我」不安。
facts.anchor: We had girl models for most of the class, but when we had our first guy model, her cheeks, her chest, and her ears all flushed hot pink.

facts.fact: 春学期第一天 Mary Ellen 的喜悦全没了、几乎不画；「我」先约她吃午饭被推辞，当天她自图书馆十五楼跳下；她的座位空着，谁也不愿坐。
facts.anchor: Later that day, she jumped off the fifteenth floor of the library.

facts.fact: 她跳楼后「我」画的每张画里都是她的脸；此前从未真正看见她——直到她在痛苦里，那时已经太晚。
facts.anchor: I hadn’t really seen her until she was in pain, and by then it was too late.

facts.fact: 同学期晚些：天主教学生协会为未出生者守夜，「我们」女性团体在草坪另一端举牌反制；两群人隔着草地静默对峙。
facts.anchor: The counterprotest was a response to the Catholic Students Association’s candlelight vigil for the unborn.

facts.fact: 草坪另一端出现不穿外套、体面流泪的 Mary Ellen；一认出她，「我」明白「夺走呼吸」是什么——气息被再见的奇迹抽走。
facts.anchor: It was Mary Ellen Bishop. The second I recognized her face, I understood what it meant that someone could take your breath away—all the air was snuffed out by the miracle of seeing her again, and I couldn’t breathe.

facts.fact: 她走近时裙摆拖过雪却不湿、不留脚印；她停在守夜者那一方——「我」明白她不是为自己而来。
facts.anchor: As she came closer, I saw that the hem of her dress trailed in the snow but didn’t get wet, and she left no footprints.

facts.fact: 唯一另一个看见她的人是蓝眼睛男人：他摇头喃喃「你不是真的」，一次比一次大声，像祈祷。
facts.anchor: You’re not real.” Then he said it again, and again, louder each time, like it was a prayer that could protect him.

facts.fact: 几天后全校传开：守夜夜崩溃的人是 Mary Ellen 的前男友 Rick Krakus——青梅竹马，据称开学前把她甩得很难看。
facts.anchor: Within a few days, everyone knew that the guy who had freaked out at the vigil was Mary Ellen’s ex-boyfriend, Rick Krakus.

facts.fact: 「我」不认为他疯了：他经历的确实是真的，只是死不肯承认。
facts.anchor: I didn’t think so. Whatever he experienced was real, but he was hell-bent on denying it.

facts.fact: 母亲从不直说这类事（或出于残留的犹太性，像避讳说 cancer）；她早早就在讲要对坏能量、酸空气敏感。
facts.anchor: But she was always saying stuff about being sensitive to bad energy or sour air, way before it was groovy.

facts.fact: 她终于承认害怕：不是怕 Mary Ellen 本身或自杀之悲，而是看见她的痛苦——太私密，像一扇窗被推开，怕有东西爬进来。
facts.anchor: It scared me. I can see that now. It wasn’t Mary Ellen herself, or even the sadness of suicide. It was witnessing her pain. It was too intimate. I felt like I had seen something I shouldn’t have, like a window had opened, and I was scared of what might crawl in.
